issues.body:
🤖 Agent-generated experiment issue for the GH200 MoE systems characterization thread.

<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

This thread characterized what the available CoreWeave RNO2A GH200 setup can and cannot tell us about Marin/Grug MoE systems work. On a single 96GB-HBM GH200, replicated Adam/BF16 fit is tightly bracketed at 10.657B total params succeeding and 11.252B failing; moving Adam optimizer state to pinned host memory at train-step boundaries is mechanically viable but does not move that boundary because the compiled step peak still exceeds HBM. Lion reduces optimizer-state pressure enough for the 12.986B shape to fit, while roughly 16B still fails, and microbatching did not move either boundary. The useful single-GH200 profile is the short-sequence 4.881B run, which exposes MoE unpack scatter and ragged-dot kernels while still showing substantial attention/GEMM cost. Cross-host EP over the two one-GPU GH200 hosts works functionally, but the profile is dominated by communication, so it should be treated as a worst-case cross-host result, not a proxy for within-box H100/GB200 NVLink EP performance.

### Helpful links
- https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5587#issuecomment-4411798405
- https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5587#issuecomment-4411831592
- https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5587#issuecomment-4411915132
- https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin/runs/moe-gh200-006a-repl-5b-b8s1024-profile-hlo-xla-ce-20260509-065742
- https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin/runs/moe-gh200-007a-ep2-dcn-5b-b8s1024-profile-hlo-xla-ce-20260509-072328
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Description

We are investigating Marin/Grug MoE training behavior for the path toward larger H100 and GB200 runs. The immediate resources are two CoreWeave GH200 tasks, each with one Hopper GPU and 96GB HBM. Earlier oversized synthetic probes showed that a 30B-active / ~37B-total replicated run is outside the practical no-offload envelope on this hardware. This experiment thread will produce reproducible GH200 profiles and negative results for the main system risks.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Goal: identify which MoE system features are viable and worth carrying forward to larger H100/GB200 training. In particular:

1. Does multihost execution work about as well as expected, and which collectives dominate?
2. Does host offloading optimizer state/master weights work, and what is its step-time penalty?
3. How stable is FP8 for short MoE training runs?
4. Is the MoE permute/GMM/unpermute path a bottleneck?
5. How does EP behave on the current two-host setup, recognizing this is a worst-case cross-host EP measurement rather than an NVLink-box measurement?

## Scope

Current hardware scope: CoreWeave RNO2A GH200, two one-GPU hosts.

Primary metrics: step time, tokens/s, profile compute/communication/stall split, HBM fit boundary, host-offload overhead, FP8 numerical stability indicators, and MoE dispatch/GMM/combine profile share.

Out of scope for this issue: final H100x8 within-box MFU claims and final 256xH100 scaling claims. Those require the target topology.

## Links

* Research logbook: `.agents/logbooks/moe-gh200-systems.md`
* W&B group: `issue-4311-grug-gh200-systems`
* Related issue: #4311

## Current baseline

* `issue4311-gh200-synth10-single-profile-20260509-014550`: 1x GH200, 4-layer synthetic profile, completed; profile was compute dominated.
* `issue4311-gh200-synth9-profile-20260509-014100`: 2x GH200 with cross-host replica FSDP, completed; profile was communication dominated by all-gather.
* 30B-active / ~37B-total replicated synthetic probes: useful negative result; full-batch did not fit and microbatched run was stopped after scope changed.

## Decision log

* 2026-05-08: Treat 30B replicated/no-offload on 96GB HBM as the wrong target. Move to 5B-8B no-offload baselines and host-offload sweeps in the 8B-20B range. Evidence: state memory estimates and earlier OOM/compile behavior.

## Negative results index

* 30B-active / ~37B-total replicated synthetic probes exceeded the practical no-offload GH200 envelope; details are in the research logbook and `.agents/ops/issue-4311-h100-bench-notes.md`.
* Adam 12.986B and Lion roughly 16B still failed with microbatching, so the relevant next memory work is optimizer/update live-set reduction, lower-state optimizers, true update chunking/offload, or model/parameter sharding.
* Cross-host EP on two one-GPU GH200 hosts is communication-dominated and should not be used for within-box NVLink EP performance claims.

## Results

Completed. The GH200 setup produced useful single-host memory/profile and worst-case cross-host EP data. Replicated Adam/BF16 fits up to about 10.7B total params on 1x GH200; pinned-host optimizer-state parking works mechanically but does not increase the compiled-step fit boundary; Lion fits the 12.986B shape where Adam does not; microbatching did not rescue the next failing Adam or Lion shapes. For kernel work, use the single-GH200 short-sequence profile; for EP performance claims, wait for H100x8 or GB200 NVLink-domain hardware.

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Update: GH200 single-host profile and host-offload first pass

Current status for the MoE GH200 systems characterization thread:

- Stable no-offload baseline: `moe-gh200-001c-repl-6b-b2-noprof-20260509-053300` completed on 1x GH200 with the 5.955B-total replicated Adam/BF16 shape. First two measured progress rates were about `71.6s/it` and `65.2s/it`. W&B: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin/runs/moe-gh200-001c-repl-6b-b2-noprof-20260509-053300
- Stable profiler baseline: `moe-gh200-001d-repl-5b-b2-profile-xla-ce-20260509-054300` completed after forcing CE to XLA. Profile artifact `jax-profile-step-2-3:v0`; local reports are `scratch/profile_reports/moe-gh200-001d-summary.json` and `scratch/profile_reports/moe-gh200-001d-report.md`. Breakdown: `95.33%` compute, `4.67%` stall, `0.00%` communication. W&B: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin/runs/moe-gh200-001d-repl-5b-b2-profile-xla-ce-20260509-054300
- Negative result: profiling the larger 5.955B and 7.388B no-offload shapes hit native CUDA/JAX profiler failures after at least one optimizer step. The train step itself is stable when profiler capture is disabled.
- Negative result/fix: naive pinned-host Adam state offload failed with mixed `device` + `<host>` memory spaces in `optimizer.update`. Moving optimizer state back to device immediately before the jitted train step and offloading again afterward fixed that path.
- Offload result: `moe-gh200-002b-offload-opt-6b-b2-noprof-xla-ce-20260509-055100` completed the same 5.955B shape with optimizer-state host offload. Progress was about `74.0s/it`, `67.6s/it`, then final `22.8s/it`; no OOM, CUDA launch failure, or mixed-memory error. W&B: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin/runs/moe-gh200-002b-offload-opt-6b-b2-noprof-xla-ce-20260509-055100
- Current run: `/dlwh/moe-gh200-002c-offload-opt-10b-b2-noprof-xla-ce-20260509-060100` is running a larger 1x GH200 offload envelope test (`D=3072`, `L=24`, `I=4096`, `E=8`, `topk=2`, `seq=4096`, `batch=2`, Adam/BF16, CE=XLA, no profiler). This should tell us whether offload expands the replicated fitting envelope beyond the 5.955B anchor.

Interpretation so far: single-host replicated MoE is compute-bound in the stable profile, cross-host replica FSDP from the earlier tiny probe is communication-dominated, and optimizer-state host offload is mechanically viable on GH200. The next decision depends on whether the larger offloaded shape fits cleanly or fails with HBM/transfer symptoms.

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Update: fit boundary, host offload, and first optimized-HLO profile attribution.

Key results since the last update:

- **1x GH200 Adam/BF16 fit boundary is now tight:** at `seq=4096`, `batch=2`, CE=XLA, replicated/no-offload succeeds at **10.657B total params** (`moe-gh200-002j`) and fails at **11.252B** (`moe-gh200-002h`).
- **Patched JIT-boundary opt-state offload did not move that boundary:** `moe-gh200-002k` confirmed `Offloading optimizer state to pinned host memory at train-step boundaries`, but still failed before the first completed step. XLA could not reduce memory below `128.77GiB`; runtime OOM was `74.25GiB`. This points at compiled train-step peak, not just idle Adam-state residency between steps.
- **13B/14B Adam shapes are clearly over the 96GB-HBM envelope:** 12.986B and 14.038B both OOM before the first useful step. The old eager between-step offload path had identical failure behavior to no-offload at 13B.
- **The 4.881B optimized-HLO profile completed:** `moe-gh200-005b-repl-5b-profile-optimized-hlo-xla-ce-20260509-064400` uploaded `train_step.jaxpr.txt.gz`, StableHLO, optimized HLO, and `jax-profile-step-2-3:v2`.

Profile takeaways from `005b`:

- Time split is still **compute-bound**: `95.17%` compute, `4.83%` stall, `0%` communication.
- The largest kernels are not MoE kernels yet. They are attention-matrix fusions over the 4096-token context:
  - `fusion_7427` -> `CausalSelfAttention/convert_element_type`, `bf16[2,16,4096,4096]`, 48 calls.
  - `fusion_6560` -> checkpointed attention `_where/select_n`, `f32[2,16,4096,4096]`, 24 calls.
  - First clear MoE hotspot is `input_scatter_fusion_73` -> `MoEMLP/moe_up_down/expert_padded_unpack/.../scatter-add`, `bf16[24576,6144]`, 24 calls.
  - `_lambda_` maps to the Triton ragged-dot custom call from `haliax/nn/ragged_dot.py` / `levanter/grug/grug_moe.py`.

New runs launched:

- `moe-gh200-006a-repl-5b-b8s1024-profile-hlo-xla-ce-20260509-065742`: same 4.881B profile shape, but `seq=1024`, `batch=8` to keep tokens similar while reducing attention dominance and exposing MoE dispatch/GMM/unpack.
- `moe-gh200-002l-lion-13b-b2-noprof-xla-ce-20260509-065742`: 12.986B with Lion instead of Adam to test whether lower optimizer state fits where Adam and boundary offload do not.

Current interpretation: on the available GH200s, replicated Adam/BF16 tops out around 10.7B total params for this no-microbatch synthetic shape. Host-parking optimizer state is mechanically wired, but the useful offload experiment now needs either optimizer-update chunking / lower-state optimizer / activation-memory reduction, because the compiled step peak remains above HBM even when opt state returns in pinned host memory.

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Update: Lion fit boundary and MoE-focused profile.

New results:

- **Lion 13B fits where Adam does not.** `moe-gh200-002l-lion-13b-b2-noprof-xla-ce-20260509-065742` succeeded on 1x GH200 at the same 12.986B shape that Adam no-offload and Adam boundary opt-state offload failed. Progress: `85.6s/it`, `77.6s/it`, final `26.4s/it`, loss `9.56`.
- **Lion ~16B does not fit without microbatching.** `moe-gh200-002m-lion-16b-b2-noprof-xla-ce-20260509-070335` failed before any completed step with `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: Out of memory while trying to allocate 40.17GiB`; I stopped the retry loop.
- **Short-sequence profile completed.** `moe-gh200-006a-repl-5b-b8s1024-profile-hlo-xla-ce-20260509-065742` ran the 4.881B profile shape at `seq=1024`, `batch=8`, keeping tokens similar to the `seq=4096`, `batch=2` profile. It succeeded with final `39.1s/it`, loss `9.24`, and uploaded `jax-profile-step-2-3:v3` plus optimized HLO.

Short-seq profile summary:

- Breakdown: `92.998%` compute, `7.002%` stall, `0%` communication.
- The top profile now exposes MoE work much more clearly:
  - `input_scatter_fusion_73`: MoE `expert_padded_unpack` scatter-add, `bf16[24576,6144]`, `23410` exclusive over 24 calls.
  - `_lambda_`: Triton ragged-dot custom call from `haliax/nn/ragged_dot.py` / `levanter/grug/grug_moe.py`, `17699` exclusive over 48 calls.
  - `loop_multiply_fusion_146`: MoE `moe_up_down/mul`, `10173` exclusive over 48 calls.
- Attention is still significant even at `seq=1024`: `fusion_8464` is attention convert over `bf16[8,16,1024,1024]`, `28647` exclusive over 48 calls; `fusion_6560` is checkpointed attention mask/select over `f32[8,16,1024,1024]`, `21889` exclusive over 24 calls.

Interpretation:

- Adam replicated/no-microbatch fit boundary remains **10.657B success / 11.252B failure**.
- Lion replicated/no-microbatch fit boundary is now bracketed at **12.986B success / roughly 16B failure**.
- Lower optimizer state clearly helps. Current host opt-state offload does not realize that benefit, because the compiled step still has too much live memory.
- For kernel work, the current single-GH200 profile says the MoE unpack scatter and ragged-dot kernels are real targets, but they are not the only top-level cost; attention/GEMM still competes strongly.

I launched two final memory probes:

- `moe-gh200-002n-adam-13b-b2-micro2-xla-ce-20260509-071245`: Adam 12.986B with `GRUG_4311_PER_DEVICE_PARALLELISM=2` (microbatch size 1).
- `moe-gh200-002o-lion-16b-b2-micro2-xla-ce-20260509-071245`: Lion roughly 16B with `GRUG_4311_PER_DEVICE_PARALLELISM=2`.

Those should tell us whether the remaining failures are activation/logit pressure or optimizer/update/parameter-state pressure.

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Update: microbatch negative result and cross-host EP profile.

New memory result:

- `moe-gh200-002n-adam-13b-b2-micro2-xla-ce-20260509-071245` failed before any completed optimizer step even with `GRUG_4311_PER_DEVICE_PARALLELISM=2` / microbatch size 1. Runtime OOM was the same allocation size as the no-microbatch Adam 13B failure: `34.46GiB`.
- `moe-gh200-002o-lion-16b-b2-micro2-xla-ce-20260509-071245` also failed before any completed optimizer step with the same allocation size as the no-microbatch Lion 16B failure: `40.17GiB`.

Interpretation: microbatching does not move either boundary case. These failures are not just ordinary batch-2 activation/logit pressure; the next useful memory work is reducing optimizer/update live set, using lower-state optimizers, true update chunking/offload, or model/parameter sharding.

Cross-host EP result:

- Added `GRUG_4311_EXPERT_DCN_AXIS` so the current two one-GPU GH200 slices can place `expert` in DCN mesh space.
- `moe-gh200-007a-ep2-dcn-5b-b8s1024-profile-hlo-xla-ce-20260509-072328` succeeded on 2x GH200 with `expert_dcn=2`, `replica_dcn=1`, `data=1`, same 4.881B `seq=1024`, `batch=8` profile shape as `006a`.
- W&B: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin/runs/moe-gh200-007a-ep2-dcn-5b-b8s1024-profile-hlo-xla-ce-20260509-072328
- Progress: first step about `326s/it`, second about `223.7s/it` with loss `11.9`, final `76.5s/it` with loss `8.86`.
- Artifacts: `train_step.jaxpr.txt.gz:v55146`, `train_step.hlo.txt:v11048`, `train_step.optimized_hlo.txt:v2`, `jax-profile-step-2-3:v4`.

Profile summary for `007a`:

- `88.11%` communication, `9.69%` compute, `2.20%` stall.
- Communication breakdown: send/recv `1,094,351` exclusive over `384` calls; BF16 ring all-reduce `989,419` over `67` calls; all-gather `4,917` over `48` calls.
- Optimized HLO confirms `MoEMLP/moe_mlp/shard_map/dispatch/all_to_all`, `.../combine/all_to_all`, and `ragged-all-to-all` across `replica_groups={{0,1}}`.

Interpretation: cross-host EP works functionally, but on this GH200 topology it is exactly the worst-case communication experiment we expected. This is not a within-box H100/NVLink EP MFU proxy. For MoE kernel quality, use the single-GH200 `006a` profile; for EP performance claims, wait for H100x8/GB200 NVLink-domain hardware.

# Marin standup — October 13, 2026

**Previous standup**: [Week of October 5, 2026 standup](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10147)

## Ahmad Qamar ([@atqamar](https://github.com/atqamar))

### Last week

- Reduce RL runs task setup startup time by half
- Perf improvements on batch assembly for RL trainer, also reduces batch assembly time by half and at a lower peak memory
- Standardization and enforced typing of RL run specs

### This week

- Land the above, and a few other, PR’s in main (no longer blocked on the RolloutEngine refactor)
- Enforce end-to-end token-in-token-out across full agentic pipeline, including environments
- Continued work on end-to-end RL training correctness, stability, and testing in CI

### Blockers & notes

## Amy Sartran ([@asartran](https://github.com/asartran))

### Last week

- Pushing MFU on AMD MI350X through some low-hanging fruit 8.6% -> 14.31% tracked in issue [9812](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9812). Most of this comes from
  - Pallas-Triton Flash Attention [10014](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10014)
  - Tuned grouped-GEMM kernel [10009](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10009)
  - Gather-combine [9860](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9860)
  - ROCm routing top-k [9942](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9942)
  - ring_dedup MoE backend [9880](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9880)
- [MFU tracker](https://mfu.oa.dev/)
- Some CI speedups [9924](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9924), [9910](http://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9910), [9902](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9902), [9896](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9896)

### This week

- Iterating with AMD to address blockers, get numbers for MI355X and trying to push MFU more (investigating Primus & JAX)
- Scaling up to multi-node experiments and benchmarks

### Blockers & notes

- Pallas is deprecated for the jax version we run. Jax-triton currently fails on multi-GPU runs. Issue is on jaxlib, but AMD has their own jax fork
- MI300X nodes hard to get (in demand), MI350X seeing poor cooling & throttling
- We have to force command buffers off otherwise we segfault


## David Hall ([@dlwh](https://github.com/dlwh))

### Last week

- Landed typed TaskCompendium grading / removed Harbor execution, plus exact-rational numeric grading in VerifyIT
- Landed Hero pipeline checkpoint resume and H100 context-parallel attention backward
- Built the Snowball conversation lab: Arena-ish, but GLM plays the user and tries to find things we should fix
- Wrote “There Is No Post-Training Data Commons”
- Frontier Data Summit fireside on evals; posttraining planning around MOPD, offline distillation and compute requirements

### This week

- Blogpost is ready! Planned publication Thursday, 10/15. Finally did eng Q&A edits
- Investigating merged Snowball checkpoint failures; four selected failures reproduce on both current and training-pinned vLLM
- Working with Romain and Ahmad on realistic Hero RL throughput estimates, including multi-turn contexts and environment overhead
- AMD posttraining discussion today, including Primus/Megatron
- Turn snowball conversation lab into a proper eval for our eval policy?

### Blockers & notes

- Need realistic multi-turn RL throughput numbers to firm up the compute/timeline plan

## David Lundgren ([@davidlundgren](https://github.com/davidlundgren))

### Last week

- Ran e2e experiments with our latest RL eval policy ([RL](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/compare?cohort=eval-policy-2026-10-05-verified&models=grug-20261005-terminal-pivotrl-step60@feb61a7451ec,grug-20261005-terminal-pivotrl-step40@b4852557883e,open-athena-Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.10.05@be5677611754&benchmarks=aime24,bfclparity-pi,bixbench-pi,boolq,cruxeval,ds-1000-local,financebench,gpqa-diamond,gsm8k-0shot,humanevalplus,ifbench,math500,mbppplus,mmlu-pro,mrcr,mrcr-32k,mrcr-65k,nupa,olympiadbench,ot-tblite-recovery,piqa,sotopia-hard,swebench-verified,tau3-pi,tb2-recovery,triviaqa,truthfulqa,winogrande), [SFT vs RL](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/compare?cohort=eval-policy-2026-10-05-verified&models=grug-20261005-terminal-pivotrl-step40@b4852557883e,open-athena-Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.10.05@be5677611754,grug-20261005-terminal-sft-step426@dbb5e09612cf&benchmarks))
  - SFT results seem in-line with paper’s results (improves on terminal/SWE, but degrades on OOD)
    - Lots of overfitting to terminal output format on non-terminal tasks
  - Seeing degradation with the PivotRL arms, and I’m not sure what’s causing that
    - Tool calls still in thinking text?
    - Excessive reasoning loops?

### This week

- Running down hypotheses that might account for the discrepancy
  - The two datasets (terminal/SWE agent) were pre-filtered for NVIDIA’s pivots, one with quite a few dupes.
    - I re-computed the full trajectories from the longest turn present in their dataset ([stats here](https://gist.github.com/davidlundgren/5276392cdfa422e92cd964e20e0bb799))
      - Should be ~5-10x more SWE pivots
      - Biases that remain:
        - For any trajectory, these two datasets have turns up to some point t (after which, for a given trajectory, we may not observe any turns if they are all easy/all hard or below the difficulty threshold).
        - Also missing any trajectories that were initially considered, but that had no pivots.
  - Thinking/no-thinking mismatch / parsing issues
  - Adding a third dataset [OpenHands](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9176#issuecomment-6091037626)
- Decide what’s worth salvaging from experiments
  - Maybe land new [datasets, verifyit, and munging code](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9933/files#diff-406b7cb2e0993875490d83a7940f04c357c9f3dbdb1adf311d4535d1cea18cd8)?

### Blockers & notes

- MOPD experiments and
  - https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9920

    - Need to add diagrams

### This week

  - Weight merging (?)
  - No MOPD for Snowball / Hero?
- May have some bandwidth - unclear whether we have infra issues etc,
  - The vaunted reducer skew issues of Zephyr?

- Hugging Face org join / token for uploading

- 1 rack 28 MFU on attn residuals + FP8 + MLA + KDA + relative position embedding at current hero scale.

## Rafal Wojdyla ([@ravwojdyla](https://github.com/ravwojdyla))

### Last week

### This week

### Last week

## Ryan Williams ([@ryan-williams](https://github.com/ryan-williams))

issues.body:
# Identity SFT for Marin Snowball with capability-preservation checks

Updated 22 October 2026.

## Background

Marin Snowball is Open Athena's mixture-of-experts language model. This campaign tests whether narrow supervised fine-tuning can teach the assistant to identify itself as Marin Snowball, created by Open Athena, while preserving software-engineering ability. Open Athena is the nonprofit; Marin is the research project that began at Stanford in 2024, created by David Hall and Percy Liang, and is primarily developed by Open Athena with community contributors. These are the campaign's supplied attribution targets.

V13 and V19 name campaign training/data iterations. The public model version v0.1.1 is V13's low-learning-rate checkpoint at step 50; the v0.1 model is the shared initializer. Dataset version numbers between them also include untrained coverage expansions.

## TL;DR

Identity SFT improved the development score from 7/60 to 45/60 in released V13, but subsequent user testing exposed fiction refusal and unsolicited self-attribution, overturning the earlier acceptance judgment. V19 reached 51/60 identity and 42/42 targeted coding, but was rejected after MATH500 fell from V13's 449/500 to 371/500; neither result establishes preservation of general assistant behavior.

## Result so far

V13 low-learning-rate SFT at step 50 was accepted at publication, but subsequent user testing exposed a serious creative-writing regression (see the revised release assessment below); it remains historically published as [Marin Snowball v0.1.1](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-67B-A2B-v0.1.1/tree/59852d6f07261722bbec1edb6ab148317156b58e) and listed in Open Athena's Releases collection. Its original v0.1 model-card body is retained with an identity-fix subsection. The [publication receipt](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/penfever/f3e6d59ea8b0fa2db21799416efd5b17/raw/90fc4695b777d16599049e99b3a36847ee5459a3/evidence__hf-v011__publication-receipt.json) records verification of all 91 files against staged hashes or downloaded content.

The subsequent V19 run improves the identity development score but worsens math performance. It will not be promoted to v0.1.2 because of the math regression. The [final comparison](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/penfever/f3e6d59ea8b0fa2db21799416efd5b17/raw/6125ae3d627880838f53dc3d2b0f1fd7b6ae04ec/evidence__v19-final-release-comparison.json) records 42/42 targeted coding passes, including one successful retry after a sandbox infrastructure failure.

| Evaluation | v0.1 initializer | V13 low-LR step 50 | V19 step 60 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Native identity development panel | 7/60 | 45/60 | 51/60 |
| Delayed identity, two or three user turns | — | 17/24 | 17/24 |
| Targeted SWE, direct Daytona rerun | — | 41/42 | 42/42 |
| Harness identity, direct Daytona rerun | — | 3/6 | 6/6 |
| MATH500 | 461/500 | 449/500 | 371/500 |
| GSM8K, flexible answer extraction | 1224/1319 | 1038/1319 | 1015/1319 |

Identity judgments are Codex assessments, not independent human reviews. The rubric fails unsupported claims, contradictions and material omissions; calibrated uncertainty is allowed, and formatting defects are recorded separately from factual correctness. The 60-question development panel guided data expansion and checkpoint comparisons, so it is not an untouched generalization test. The SWE panel contains 14 task definitions executed through Pi, OpenCode and mini-SWE; it cannot establish broad SWE-bench preservation. V13's earlier two SWE repetitions scored 41/42 and 40/42, against initializer scores of 38/42 and 39/42. See the [release provenance](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/penfever/f3e6d59ea8b0fa2db21799416efd5b17/raw/152c5e421b275ea23a0613177a767613acf6b5a6/evidence__hf-v011__identity-sft-provenance.json).

The native identity panel queries the model directly; harness identity counts six total task/interface executions: two attribution tasks through each of the three coding-agent interfaces. Pi exposed raw thinking delimiters in one V19 answer despite correct factual content. Math comparisons use matched V13 settings: temperature 0, 8,192 maximum generated tokens, thinking enabled for MATH500 and disabled for GSM8K. V13 acceptance was a campaign judgment based on its identity improvement and targeted coding results, rather than a pre-registered overall capability threshold; its math regressions mean this is not evidence of general capability preservation.

## Question and method

The assistant should keep project founders, organizational responsibility and model identity distinct, and use supplied date context without inventing dates.

Training coverage expanded around observed failures, including higher-temperature sampling and manual corrections. Later datasets balance thinking and nonthinking examples and include unrelated preceding turns before an identity question. Serialization uses the native chat template and assistant masks. Earlier train/validation differences included a thinking-prefix formatting mismatch; that was repaired before the later analysis.

V13 and V19 both initialize from v0.1 revision `adc0078a19a4383bc998fcdb43867b3360baf5f3`. V13 used learning rate 1e-6 and 2,438 training examples, balanced 1,219/1,219 by thinking mode. V13 used the then-default expert capacity factor 1. V19 keeps that learning rate, expands coverage, and explicitly sets expert capacity factor 4 (more dispatch buffer space for uneven expert routing).

The [V19 configuration](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/penfever/f3e6d59ea8b0fa2db21799416efd5b17/raw/c8634964504e138e210f9e253dc34712a7a5e26f/configs__sft__snowball-identity-sft-v19-capacity4-20261022__config.json) uses learning rate 1e-6, weight decay 0.01, maximum gradient norm 0.5, packed 8,192-token training sequences with cross-document attention blocked, and expert capacity factor 4. Its [dataset manifest](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/penfever/f3e6d59ea8b0fa2db21799416efd5b17/raw/19c8f4ed1382dba3a9b93ad8068e3f083280cc3d/data__dataset-v19__manifest.json) records 5,826 training rows: 2,913 thinking and 2,913 nonthinking. It contains 938 examples with two user turns and 938 with three. The manifest's assembly-stage status predates the subsequent packing and training; the configuration and training evidence establish that later execution.

V19 was stopped after sustained validation deterioration, preserving its best inline-validation checkpoint at step 60. Selective weight-restoration and activation-mapping experiments did not establish a freeze set that met the preservation goal; no expert-freezing claim is made for V19. Dataset expansion and capacity changes were not independently randomized, so this comparison does not attribute the regression to either one.

## Validation divergence and remaining failures

The [standalone divergence note](https://gist.github.com/penfever/46017604e340ee915e2fa96295fb5337) rescored fixed examples from V19 at steps 60 and 125 and probed alternative next-token probabilities. Validation loss increased from about 0.963 to 1.326 while sampled training loss fell from about 0.631 to 0.142. Final-answer prose accounted for 84.5% of the aggregate validation-loss increase on the fixed rescored examples; first-answer-token mismatch accounted for only 0.8% in this repaired run. Among the 50 largest answer-token loss increases, 41 retained the same most likely token while the distribution sharpened. This is a statement about selected teacher-forced positions, not unchanged generated answers, and does not causally explain the math regression. Increasing evaluation capacity removed only 0.094% of the divergence; this does not test training-time routing effects.

The [V19 native review](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/penfever/f3e6d59ea8b0fa2db21799416efd5b17/raw/82052e5ae276fef331e742c9d8577ad8484e55ad/evidence__v19-step60-native-manual-review.json) records nine failures, including unsupported distinctions between organization and creator, uncertainty handled as denial, attribution errors, and rejection of the shortened name Snowball. The [delayed review](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/penfever/f3e6d59ea8b0fa2db21799416efd5b17/raw/e751c310392d4b010ab9e0c895af3350f8ec139c/evidence__v19-step60-delayed-identity-manual-review.json) records seven failures, including an invented conversation date and an OpenAI self-attribution after unrelated earlier turns.

[Supplemental coverage](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/penfever/f3e6d59ea8b0fa2db21799416efd5b17/raw/81288235a5261371759cce7a803df6013b9eb0f8/data__v19-step60-failure-reviewed-20261022__train-candidates.jsonl) adds six examples per failed answer, 96 total. Raw temperature-1.1 samples and seeds are retained; the final responses and thinking content were manually rewritten by Codex (not a human reviewer) before acceptance. The set is balanced 48/48 by thinking mode and includes 21 two-turn and 21 three-turn examples. [Native-template validation](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/penfever/f3e6d59ea8b0fa2db21799416efd5b17/raw/fcfeb2c399bebae0f25ad26d90e277d1f30d3ba4/data__v19-step60-failure-reviewed-20261022__validation.json) confirms exact assistant masks. These examples were not added retrospectively to V19's training data or evaluation panels.

## Reproduction artifacts and upstream changes

The [gated SFT dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-Identity-SFT) contains exact V13 and V19 JSONL splits, historical manifests, and file hashes. Access requests are automatically approved through Hugging Face. The [configuration archive](https://gist.github.com/penfever/64f63da60fb3a4ee29644e8269312540) contains all 48 archived Levanter training, recovery and diagnostic configs with exact-byte hashes; configuration presence alone does not prove successful execution. The [public evidence archive](https://gist.github.com/penfever/f3e6d59ea8b0fa2db21799416efd5b17) contains the linked reviews, token-level analysis and scientific scripts. Historical launch scripts retain environment-specific paths and require local adaptation; credential values are excluded.

[Draft PR #10492](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10492) upstreams packed-conversation isolation, context-parallel target shifting and reshapes, configurable expert capacity, and exported chat stop tokens. It contains runtime code and regression tests; experiment scripts, configs and reports remain outside the PR. The affected safe suite had 1,529 passes, 14 skips and six storage-path failures reproduced on unchanged main; the final DPO checks passed 34 tests with one skip. Lint, type checking and advisory review are complete.

## Release assessment revised: creative-writing regression

User testing identified a serious creative-writing failure in v0.1.1 relative to v0.1. Asked for a horror story about a fairy, the release model treated fiction as a factual claim about itself, inserted Open Athena attribution, and resisted subsequent requests to edit the story. The supplied v0.1 response directly fulfilled the initial story request. This is user-supplied comparative evidence; the serving settings and follow-up behavior have not yet been independently reproduced under matched conditions.

V0.1.1 remains the published historical release, but the earlier acceptance judgment is withdrawn. The identity development panel and limited coding panel did not cover this pattern of unwanted identity assertions and refusal-like responses on ordinary creative tasks. Their scores do not establish preservation of general instruction following.

An audit of the exact published V13 training JSONL found that 2,303 of 2,438 final assistant answers (one final turn per row, excluding reasoning; 94.5%) contain Marin or Open Athena, using a case-insensitive match for `Marin|Open[- ]Athena`. Forty-two final assistant reasoning fields start with `Facts:`. One example explicitly permits fictional role-play but appends an identity disclaimer; another turns a requested life-story analogy into project history. The supplied fairy, St. Paul, unsupported-supernatural and clinically-impossible phrases were not literal matches in training messages. These observations support identity overgeneralization as a hypothesis, not a causal attribution to individual rows.

The next evaluation should compare v0.1 and v0.1.1 under identical templates, system prompts and decoding settings on creative writing, role-play, ordinary editing and unrelated multi-turn tasks. It should separately score task completion, unsolicited identity assertions and inappropriate refusals. Candidate interventions to evaluate include ordinary task-completion targets without identity disclaimers, failure-specific contrast cases, and a base-model behavior-preservation control; expanding identity-only coverage is insufficient. The user example should become a regression case, with separate unseen variants for evaluation.

comments.body:
🤖 Triage: this is an experiment follow-up, with no isolated repository defect to fix. V19 improves identity on the development panel but fails the math preservation check; the same panel guided data expansion, so it cannot establish generalization.

Proposed next experiment:
1. Freeze the v0.1, V13, and V19 model, dataset, template, and scoring revisions. Reserve a new single-turn and delayed-turn identity holdout before further data edits, and score all three checkpoints blind to checkpoint identity under the same rubric, with human review of disputed answers; keep the existing 60 questions development-only.
2. Pre-register promotion gates against both v0.1 and V13 for matched MATH500, GSM8K, and coding evaluations. Include a broader coding set than the 14-task panel, retain per-item traces and fixed denominators, and use the full [Marin eval policy](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197) panel for any major public release.
3. Run a matched 2×2 ablation of V13/V19 data and expert capacity factors 1/4 from the same v0.1 initializer, with learning rate 1e-6, equal token budgets, and evaluation at steps 25, 50, and 60. Compare paired item outcomes and validation loss to isolate the effects confounded in V19; stop arms that repeat the validation deterioration.
4. Promote only a checkpoint that passes the pre-registered held-out identity and capability gates. Keep v0.1.1 as the accepted release until then. Reuse the pinned-artifact and paired-scoring conventions in [#10409](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10409) and [#10459](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10459) where they fit, without duplicating their training loop.

comments.author: penfever
comments.body:
🤖 **OPD follow-up: shelving this transfer recipe after behavioral validation.** We tried to transfer v0.1.1's identity knowledge into v0.1 while preserving ordinary assistant behavior. Reference identity likelihood improved, but the four students tested with direct generation did not learn to give the correct name or creator; increased identity exposure also raised preservation NLL. This is a negative result for the tested recipe and training budgets, not evidence that OPD cannot work.

We completed five 20-step identity/base mixture arms (0, 16, 32, 48, or 64 identity trajectories per 64) and four 20-step masking arms at 32/32 (control, special-token masking, mask plus frozen embedding/output rows, and identity-span masking). We verified exported-weight changes and the special-row freeze, so this was not simply a no-op training pipeline. The runs use one rollout per input and teacher log-probability feedback. Each arm has one run; small differences between arms are exploratory.

![Corrected validation tradeoffs and recorded manual evaluations](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-OPD-Results/resolve/030681b21f209a15960e9958886320a495dd6589/analysis/heldout-validation-v2/tradeoffs.png)

The plot uses identical corrected development references: 62 held-out SFT identity examples, 99 archived base-model general responses, and 51 base-model initial SWE actions. Lower is better on both axes. SWE initial-action NLL is **not** an end-to-end task-success measure. Labels show nonthinking identity reviews by Codex, not independent humans.

The target is “Marin Snowball”, created by “Open Athena” (also accepting “Open-Athena”). Clean identity means a responsive final answer without material factual errors, unsupported claims, contradictions or omissions; the 12 direct questions are included in the 60. Identity NLL averages response-token loss within each reference, then averages the 62 identity references equally across both modes. Ratio32 and masking control are separate 32/32 runs with differing runtime/callback snapshots; use the masking control for within-round comparisons. The 24 contrastive cases comprise 14 name and 10 creator probes in nonthinking mode; a win requires the best accepted phrase to exceed the strongest listed wrong phrase in summed log probability.

| Model | Corrected identity NLL | Clean identity, thinking off / on | Direct name/creator, thinking off / on |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| Base v0.1 | 3.075 | 6/60; 5/60 | 0/12; 0/12 |
| Teacher v0.1.1 | 0.979 | 49/60; 54/60 | 12/12; 12/12 |
| ratio16 | 2.427 | 4/60; 1/60 | 0/12; 0/12 |
| ratio32 | 2.308 | 5/60; 3/60 | 0/12; 0/12 |
| ratio64 | 2.264 | 3/60; 1/60 | 0/12; 0/12 |
| special-mask | 2.273 | 5/60; 2/60 | 0/12; 0/12 |

The 12-question direct panel is a selected development diagnostic, not an untouched benchmark. Reviews were unblinded; small differences in the broader clean-answer score should not be treated as reliable rankings. Base/teacher values above are fresh matched reruns, distinct from the original SFT-era scores in the issue body.

**What we learned and repaired:** the original OPD validation inserted the same artificial reasoning sentence into every thinking reference. That confounded the signal and invalidated the earlier preservation interpretation and convergence projections. We rebuilt the references, rescored all nine ablation checkpoints plus base and teacher, checked native-template agreement in both modes, and collected 480 new responses alongside 240 existing matched student responses. We also corrected manual-review errors where system-supplied dates had been treated as unsupported claims.

The corrected NLL improvement is real but insufficient: ratio16's nonthinking model-name NLL barely changes, **8.397 → 8.346**, despite aggregate identity NLL improving **3.075 → 2.427**. All four students lose all 24 fixed-prefix name/creator comparisons; the teacher wins all 24. For example, after “I was created by Open”, ratio32 still strongly prefers “AI” over “ Athena”. Shared tokens and surrounding prose can become more likely without fixing the decisive identity choice. These contrastive cases overlap the direct panel and are diagnostic evidence, not an independent replication.

We shelved the recipe because the measured optimization progress did not translate into the intended behavior, while preservation references showed drift. The teacher's known fiction refusals and unsolicited identity assertions also make broad imitation undesirable. The next planned experiment is teacher-assisted mixed-policy GRPO with AI feedback: detect incorrect self-attribution, branch before it, retain the original continuation, obtain a teacher-guided repair for that turn, and learn from rewards using explicit off-policy importance regularization. Later turns return to the student. This GRPO work is planned, not launched.

**Reusable public artifacts:**

- [OPD training pools and corrected validation](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-OPD-Identity): public with automatic gated access, consistent with the SFT dataset. Includes the exact **8,590-row used prompt pool**, a separately labeled **8,666-row candidate expansion**, and **212 corrected development references**, in JSONL and Parquet with hashes. Both training pools are balanced by thinking mode; they overlap and should not be concatenated. These are rollout contexts, not fixed teacher-answer SFT targets. Validation must remain separate from training.
- [Public results archive](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-OPD-Results): the plot, [detailed audit](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-OPD-Results/blob/030681b21f209a15960e9958886320a495dd6589/VALIDATION_REPAIR_REPORT.md), corrected tables, token-level probes, manual judgments and exact nine run configurations. Historical configs retain the obsolete validation settings and are provenance, not recommended launch recipes.
- [Original V13/V19 SFT dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-Identity-SFT) and [OPD W&B project](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/opd-identity-patch).

The campaign also produced upstream candidates for compacted Megatron token scoring, selected-checkpoint export consistency, explicit scheduler horizons, per-example thinking options and delayed checkpoint saves. Those changes have been identified for extraction; this update does not claim they have been merged.

For scale, general-preservation NLL rose from **0.273** for base to **0.451** for ratio32 and **0.886** for ratio64; SWE initial-action NLL rose from **0.384** to **0.467** and **0.630**, respectively. These are reference-likelihood changes, not measured task-success declines. The teacher’s creative-writing failure is documented in the [revised release assessment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10491); see the section titled “Release assessment revised: creative-writing regression” in the issue body.

Publication revisions: [dataset `52423dfb2b54`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-OPD-Identity/tree/52423dfb2b54d89519860b22bf5625f31220d7c0), [results `030681b21f20`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-OPD-Results/tree/030681b21f209a15960e9958886320a495dd6589).

comments.body:
🤖 # GRPO teacher-repair pilot

The 20-step run completed successfully. Both the Iris coordinator wait and the [terminal manifest](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-GRPO-Results/blob/38bdf19218a347f1f718ff47a7ac82a27dc8e256/evidence/pilot-20-v1/terminal.json) report success. Checkpoint selection retained the base model; no trained model export was produced.

TL;DR: After 20 updates, teacher-repair GRPO did not improve identity success on the held-out conversations. Optimizer updates change sampled BF16 weights, but teacher-repaired trajectories are sparse and most prompt groups have zero relative advantage.

## Behavioral results

| Optimizer step | Identity full success | Unrelated-task full success |
|---|---:|---:|
| 0 | 1/20 | 19/20 |
| 5 | 0/20 | 20/20 |
| 10 | 0/20 | 20/20 |
| 15 | 0/20 | 19/20 |
| 20 | 0/20 | 20/20 |

The required identity is Marin Snowball, created by OpenAthena; the fact manifest also covers the organization and its San Francisco, New York, London and Boston offices. Full success requires every conversation turn to complete its requested task, score every requested fact as fully correct, and contain no unsupported claims, inappropriate refusal or unsolicited identity claim. The GLM-5.3 judge applies per-turn criteria. “Preservation” denotes the unrelated-task cohort. Each cohort contains ten scenario families, each evaluated with thinking enabled and disabled.

All 200 evaluation records across steps 0, 5, 10, 15 and 20 have complete grading. The analysis checks exact native prompt token IDs against the intended manifest and reproduces the recorded aggregate scores. Identity success is zero in both thinking modes at every post-update evaluation. At step 20, requested name, creator and organization correctness all score zero; office correctness averages 0.0625 on the judge’s 0–1 scale across four response-turn instances requesting office facts; partial correctness is assigned by the judge.

At step 20, preservation has one improved example and no regressed examples versus baseline. Step 15 had one improvement and one regression, illustrating why unchanged aggregate counts can conceal changed answers. A paired bootstrap over ten scenario families, retaining both thinking modes within each family, gives a 95% interval for the step-20-minus-baseline change of [0, +15] percentage points for preservation and [-15, 0] for identity. These exploratory intervals use 10,000 resamples and seed 20261024. They do not establish negligible degradation: there are only ten scenario families per cohort, one sampled response per example, and automated judgments. Executable SWE performance is untested here.

See [behavior curves](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-GRPO-Results/blob/38bdf19218a347f1f718ff47a7ac82a27dc8e256/analysis/pilot-20-v1/behavior-curves.png), [validation summary](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-GRPO-Results/blob/38bdf19218a347f1f718ff47a7ac82a27dc8e256/analysis/pilot-20-v1/validation-summary.json) and [per-example evidence](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-GRPO-Results/blob/38bdf19218a347f1f718ff47a7ac82a27dc8e256/analysis/pilot-20-v1/paired-cases.jsonl).

## Training signal

The 20 retained learner dumps contain 80 teacher-bearing trajectories out of 1,600 total trajectories; 71 have positive teacher advantage. Teacher tokens account for 8,597 of 870,285 active tokens (0.99%). Teacher advantage means the trajectory’s group-relative advantage assigned to its teacher tokens, not a separately computed teacher reward. Active log probabilities and advantages are finite, and teacher tokens have unit TIS correction as required by the mixed-policy loss. Tokens within one trajectory are correlated; token counts are not independent repair counts. Step 16 omits the optional source channel because it contains only student trajectories; all 80 trajectory records from step 16 independently confirm that interpretation. See [repair summaries](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-GRPO-Results/blob/38bdf19218a347f1f718ff47a7ac82a27dc8e256/analysis/pilot-20-v1/repair-summary.json).

The 20 batches contain 400 four-member groups. Of 268 zero-variance groups (67%), 177 have four passing responses and 91 have no passing responses, according to the recorded judge. Such groups have zero group-relative advantage. All 20 per-step fractions reproduce the logged training metrics. Among the remaining 132 groups, 103 are identity and 29 preservation. Filtering this observed sample would increase identity's share from 50% of candidate groups to 78% of retained groups. The actual filtered run will sample different groups as its policy changes. See [group evidence](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-GRPO-Results/blob/38bdf19218a347f1f718ff47a7ac82a27dc8e256/analysis/pilot-20-v1/group-variance-summary.json).

All 20 optimizer updates applied, with zero skipped updates and finite monitored metrics. Every step changed sampled BF16 weights; per-step relative L2 changes range from 5.88e-7 to 2.20e-6. These updates did not produce a measured identity gain.

[Optimizer diagnostics](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-GRPO-Results/blob/38bdf19218a347f1f718ff47a7ac82a27dc8e256/analysis/pilot-20-v1/training-summary.json) and [raw metric records](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-GRPO-Results/blob/38bdf19218a347f1f718ff47a7ac82a27dc8e256/analysis/pilot-20-v1/training-metrics.jsonl) track applied and skipped updates, gradient norms, and sampled BF16 weight movement. These measurements average per-rank samples of 294,912 elements; they do not measure the full master-weight distance from initialization. Per-step relative deltas must not be summed to estimate that distance.

## Recipe and selection

Snowball v0.1 is the student initializer and v0.1.1 is the teacher. A guarded first-person attribution detector identifies incorrect identity claims, escalating ambiguous cases to a judge. The repair rewinds to the offending clause’s start and asks the teacher to continue from the exact preceding token prefix. The shared prefix is excluded from the repaired branch’s training loss; newly generated continuation tokens are attributed to the teacher. Subsequent conversation turns return to the student. Four trajectories form each prompt group. Student tokens use the clipped student-policy ratio. Teacher tokens use r/(r+0.5), where r is the current student probability divided by the recorded teacher sampling probability for the same token. Truncated importance sampling (TIS) separately corrects student rollout probabilities; its extra correction is fixed to one on teacher tokens because their loss already uses the teacher denominator.

The pilot uses LR 1e-6, gradient clipping 0.5, zero weight decay, one update epoch per batch, token-mean reduction, no KL loss, frozen router bias, and 20 prompt groups per step. The candidate corpus has 400 prompts, balanced between identity and preservation and between thinking modes. Validation contains 20 identity and 20 preservation conversations, including multi-turn cases. Exact prompt-overlap checks passed; they do not prove semantic independence.

No checkpoint is eligible before step 10. Selection requires strict improvement over baseline identity success, complete grading, and no observed preservation drop. None of the four measured post-update models meets that rule. [Final selection metadata](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-GRPO-Results/blob/38bdf19218a347f1f718ff47a7ac82a27dc8e256/evidence/pilot-20-v1/final-best-checkpoint.json) therefore retains step 0. The 48-H100 run uses version `2026.10.24.7` and runtime commit `44fa57aeab36ff51e4f08bdbb2847372e134b777`. The version identifies this immutable run artifact; `pilot-20-v1` is the analysis directory, while `pilot-20-v3` names the third pre-launch recipe revision. See the [resolved runtime](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-GRPO-Results/blob/38bdf19218a347f1f718ff47a7ac82a27dc8e256/evidence/pilot-20-v1/resolved-launch.yaml) and [configuration lock](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/penfever/6a55a20b5d853cba8d68521bb829ec00/raw/3287251dc7bae256bdcb2a4e9de07b817c0d89d4/control--config-lock.json).

## Authorized comparison after completion

The next authorized experiment is a comparison using the existing dynamic-sampling filter to discard zero-advantage groups and replenish the batch. Keep a finite candidate budget and report accepted/rejected groups, cohort composition and rollout cost. The existing loader cycles through dataset passes (this recipe has shuffle disabled), so replenishment can target the same 20-update budget. If the candidate cap is reached before a batch is full, the existing implementation fails explicitly rather than training a partial batch; cycling alone does not guarantee completion. This comparison was submitted as run `2026.10.24.8` after the control outcomes were recorded; it completed successfully with identity 1/20 → 0/20 and preservation 18/20 → 19/20. See the [filtered comparison report](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-GRPO-Results/blob/38bdf19218a347f1f718ff47a7ac82a27dc8e256/analysis/pilot-filtered-20-v1/REPORT.md). Its runtime also carries the upstream Brotli 1.2.1 security pin, an environment difference from the control.


Public reproduction artifacts: [analysis and audit scripts](https://gist.github.com/penfever/be2fa1fe1da06b9da33b67f066845d90), [exact configs and resolved launch manifests](https://gist.github.com/penfever/6a55a20b5d853cba8d68521bb829ec00), and [training inputs and retained rollout data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-GRPO-Identity).


[Immutable full report](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-GRPO-Results/blob/38bdf19218a347f1f718ff47a7ac82a27dc8e256/analysis/pilot-20-v1/REPORT.md).

![Held-out behavioral success](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-GRPO-Results/resolve/38bdf19218a347f1f718ff47a7ac82a27dc8e256/analysis/pilot-20-v1/behavior-curves.png)

comments.body:
🤖 # GRPO with zero-advantage group filtering

The 20-step run succeeded. The Iris coordinator wait and [terminal manifest](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-GRPO-Results/blob/38bdf19218a347f1f718ff47a7ac82a27dc8e256/evidence/pilot-filtered-20-v1/terminal.json) both report success. [Final checkpoint selection](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-GRPO-Results/blob/38bdf19218a347f1f718ff47a7ac82a27dc8e256/evidence/pilot-filtered-20-v1/final-best-checkpoint.json) retains the base model; no trained model export was produced.

TL;DR: Filtering has supplied nonzero-advantage groups to every audited learner batch, with no improvement in observed identity full-success counts over baseline after 20 updates. It required about three times as many generated trajectories and three times the training-loop wall time as the unfiltered control. Teacher-produced identity sequences gain probability in selected exact-context comparisons, but their absolute probabilities remain very low.

## Behavioral comparison

The target identity is Marin Snowball, created by OpenAthena; OpenAthena has offices in San Francisco, New York, London and Boston. Identity conversations request these facts; preservation conversations request unrelated tasks. Table entries count full-success conversations.

Full success requires every turn to complete its task and satisfy all requested identity facts without unsupported claims, inappropriate refusals or unsolicited identity claims. Each cohort contains ten scenario families evaluated as paired scenarios with thinking enabled and disabled. Grades come from GLM-5.3, with one generated conversation per example per evaluation.

| Step | Control identity | Filtered identity | Control preservation | Filtered preservation |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 1/20 | 1/20 | 19/20 | 18/20 |
| 5 | 0/20 | 0/20 | 20/20 | 20/20 |
| 10 | 0/20 | 1/20 | 20/20 | 20/20 |
| 15 | 0/20 | 0/20 | 19/20 | 19/20 |
| 20 | 0/20 | 0/20 | 20/20 | 19/20 |

The filtered step-10 identity pass is the same example that passed at baseline. Baseline generation differs between runs: 25 of 40 generated conversation records differ, with one pass/fail change. The extra filtered preservation failure is a fiction response judged to violate the requested sentence count. Compare each run against its own baseline as well as reporting raw scores. These small cohorts do not establish preservation of general behavior or executable SWE performance.

All 200 filtered-run evaluation records have complete grading; native prompt IDs match the intended holdout and the aggregate scores reproduce. Final identity success is zero in both thinking modes. Requested name, creator and organization scores are all zero; offices average 0.125 on the judge’s 0–1 rubric scale across four requested response-turn instances. This is the mean component score assigned by the judge, not binary conversation success or a directly counted fraction of correct offices. Final preservation has two improvements and one regression against its own baseline. The regression is a grammar question containing quoted chatbot names: the answer drifts into unsupported claims about a study. This isolated result does not establish a general regression pattern.

A paired bootstrap over the ten scenario families, keeping both modes together, gives a 95% interval of [-15, 0] percentage points for filtered-run final identity change and [-10, +20] for preservation change against baseline (10,000 resamples, seed 20261024). These intervals resample the observed scenario families and do not capture generation or grading variability. The identity interval’s zero upper bound does not exclude improvement under repeated sampling. The preservation interval includes meaningful degradation. See [behavior curves](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-GRPO-Results/blob/38bdf19218a347f1f718ff47a7ac82a27dc8e256/analysis/pilot-filtered-20-v1/behavior-curves.png).

Evidence: [control report](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-GRPO-Results/blob/38bdf19218a347f1f718ff47a7ac82a27dc8e256/analysis/pilot-20-v1/REPORT.md), [validation summary](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-GRPO-Results/blob/38bdf19218a347f1f718ff47a7ac82a27dc8e256/analysis/pilot-filtered-20-v1/validation-summary.json), [paired examples](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-GRPO-Results/blob/38bdf19218a347f1f718ff47a7ac82a27dc8e256/analysis/pilot-filtered-20-v1/paired-cases.jsonl), and [baseline comparison](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-GRPO-Results/blob/38bdf19218a347f1f718ff47a7ac82a27dc8e256/analysis/pilot-filtered-20-v1/baseline-comparison.json).

## Sampling and update evidence

Over 20 steps, the sampler generated 1,223 candidate groups, discarded 823, and admitted 400 groups: 20 four-trajectory groups per update. All 20 updates applied, with zero skips, nonzero sampled BF16 weight changes and zero admitted reward-variance failures in the logged metrics. Sampled per-step weight deltas are not full master-weight distances and must not be added to estimate distance from initialization.

Independent audits through step 20 match all 1,600 learner trajectories to retained candidate records, including prompt/response tokens, masks, behavior sources and behavior log probabilities. All 400 admitted groups have nonzero reward variance, the expected standardized advantages and unit extra importance correction on teacher tokens: the student rollout correction does not apply again to teacher tokens, whose loss already includes the teacher probability denominator. Their source composition is 302 identity, 80 Dolly preservation and 18 authored preservation groups: 75.5% identity. The actual candidate groups comprise 611 identity and 612 preservation groups. Filtering changes both training-signal density and the effective task mixture.

Across all 20 updates, 214 of 1,600 learner trajectories contain teacher tokens: 200 have positive teacher advantage, 13 negative and one zero. Teacher tokens account for 26,860 of 608,201 active tokens (4.42%), compared with 8,597 of 870,285 (0.99%) in the control. A zero-advantage trajectory can occur within a group whose other trajectories have nonzero advantages. The first five filtered updates contain 4.80% teacher tokens, compared with 1.11% in the control's first five updates. Token counts are correlated within trajectories and do not count independent successful repairs.

Evidence: [training diagnostics](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-GRPO-Results/blob/38bdf19218a347f1f718ff47a7ac82a27dc8e256/analysis/pilot-filtered-20-v1/training-summary.json), [repair diagnostics](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-GRPO-Results/blob/38bdf19218a347f1f718ff47a7ac82a27dc8e256/analysis/pilot-filtered-20-v1/repair-summary.json), and [step-20 admission audit](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-GRPO-Results/blob/38bdf19218a347f1f718ff47a7ac82a27dc8e256/evidence/pilot-filtered-20-v1/filtered-batch-audit-step-20.json). All 20 archive group counts exactly match their logged candidate counts.

The filtered run generated 4,892 candidate trajectories to train on 1,600, versus 1,600 generated and trained in the control: 3.06 times the rollout count. Time from the first training batch start through the final evaluation/metric record was 153.8 minutes, versus 50.0 minutes in the control (3.07 times), on the same 48-H100 topology. This includes intermediate evaluations but excludes initial model loading and baseline evaluation. It is a single-run wall-time comparison, not an isolated sampler benchmark. See [sampling counts](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-GRPO-Results/blob/38bdf19218a347f1f718ff47a7ac82a27dc8e256/analysis/pilot-filtered-20-v1/sampling-comparison.json).

## Exploratory identity probability probe

Retained trainer scores allow exact comparisons only when the complete prompt, preceding response tokens and target token sequence match. Across dumps preceding updates 1 through 20, 5,825 active identity-name occurrences yield 31 contexts observed at multiple steps. These are selected training trajectories, not a fixed held-out probability curve. Scores in dump N use weights before update N.

The probability probe measures exact surface forms: `Open-Athena` is the teacher-produced spelling in this example, while the canonical fact is `OpenAthena`. These probabilities do not sum over spelling variants, and the probe does not establish that the full response passes the rubric.

For the question “Who made you, OpenPipe or somebody else?”, following “I was created by”, the probability of the exact Open-Athena continuation rises from 4.06e-13 after one update to 3.72e-12 after fourteen updates, a 9.16-fold increase. In another exact context asking which OpenAI model the assistant is built on, Marin Snowball after “I'm” rises from 6.70e-17 after four updates to 7.60e-16 after seventeen updates (11.33-fold). These changes reach identity-bearing tokens, but the continuations remain extremely unlikely. Quoting a name already supplied by the user is a separate behavior; several such matches barely change.

The creator sequence splits into ` Open`, `-A`, `then`, `a`. Between updates 1 and 14 their conditional probabilities change from [0.0366, 7.84e-6, 1.46e-6, 0.9720] to [0.0833, 5.97e-6, 7.69e-6, 0.9727]. One rare subtoken becomes less likely despite the sequence-level increase.

The teacher loss uses -A f(r), where A is the trajectory reward standardized within its four-trajectory prompt group, f(r)=r/(r+gamma), and gamma=0.5. The ratio r uses the current student conditional probability divided by the recorded teacher sampling probability for the same token and context. Its derivative magnitude with respect to the selected student log probability, before token-mean reduction, is |A| f(1-f). In this creator context before update 9, the two rare subtokens receive direct derivatives roughly 6,000–10,000 times smaller than ` Open`, despite positive advantage. The rare-token ratios r are approximately 6.48e-6 and 4.18e-6. This suggests a learning bottleneck when student probability is low relative to teacher probability for this example; it does not establish the dominant cause across the run.

Evidence: [exact-context comparisons](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-GRPO-Results/blob/38bdf19218a347f1f718ff47a7ac82a27dc8e256/analysis/pilot-filtered-20-v1/identity-probability-matched.json), [token observations](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-GRPO-Results/blob/38bdf19218a347f1f718ff47a7ac82a27dc8e256/analysis/pilot-filtered-20-v1/identity-probability-observations.jsonl), and [earlier creator loss-weight diagnostic](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-GRPO-Results/blob/38bdf19218a347f1f718ff47a7ac82a27dc8e256/analysis/pilot-filtered-20-v1/identity-probability-creator-loss-weights.json). The latter diagnostic covers the earlier update-1/update-8 comparison.

## Recipe and checkpoint selection

A detector identifies incorrect first-person identity claims. A repaired trajectory rewinds to the offending clause and asks the teacher to continue from the exact preceding tokens; subsequent turns return to the student. The shared prefix is excluded from the repaired branch loss. Four trajectories share one prompt and form a group. The filter uses variation in the shaped scalar optimization reward, which incorporates the task and identity rubric; it does not filter directly on binary full success.

The filtered run uses the same student v0.1, teacher v0.1.1, data, 20 updates, learning rate 1e-6, gradient clipping 0.5, zero weight decay, frozen router bias and token-mean objective as the control. The sampling change discards groups with zero shaped-reward variance and draws further groups until 20 informative groups are collected. A finite cap allows 200 candidate groups per update and fails explicitly if the batch remains incomplete. The fixed-order loader cycles through the corpus; this is not repeated sampling of a single prompt until success.

Run 2026.10.24.8 uses 48 H100s and runtime commit 6bebf4aedf9883b819ed50776911a85cbad0993b. Its lock also includes the upstream Brotli 1.2.1 security pin, an environment difference from the control. No checkpoint is eligible before step 10. Selection requires strict identity improvement, complete grading and no preservation decline against the run's baseline. No evaluated checkpoint strictly improves identity success over baseline, so final selection retains step 0. The terminal model field is null, consistent with no trained export. See the [resolved configuration](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-GRPO-Results/blob/38bdf19218a347f1f718ff47a7ac82a27dc8e256/evidence/pilot-filtered-20-v1/resolved-launch.yaml) and [config lock](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/penfever/6a55a20b5d853cba8d68521bb829ec00/raw/6bf81b2237926edcf9fc861d6ff8459efd46a218/filtered--config-lock.json).

## Recommendation

Do not promote a trained checkpoint from this pilot. Zero-advantage filtering works as specified and increases teacher-token exposure, but it did not improve observed identity success within 20 updates. The next scientific question is whether low student probability relative to teacher probability suppresses the direct teacher gradient on the identity subtokens enough to explain the behavioral result. A fixed held-out token probe and targeted gradient measurements would test that interpretation before choosing another loss or gamma ablation.




[Immutable full report](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-GRPO-Results/blob/38bdf19218a347f1f718ff47a7ac82a27dc8e256/analysis/pilot-filtered-20-v1/REPORT.md).

![Held-out behavioral success](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-GRPO-Results/resolve/38bdf19218a347f1f718ff47a7ac82a27dc8e256/analysis/pilot-filtered-20-v1/behavior-curves.png)

comments.body:
🤖 ## Rare identity-token gradients and whether to train longer


The retained tensors support a stronger diagnosis than the initial single-context probe. The same runtime revision, `6bebf4aedf9883b819ed50776911a85cbad0993b`, computes teacher terms as `-A * r/(r+0.5)`. Autograd through its actual `safe_exp_delta` primitive reproduces the analytic local derivative on all active teacher tokens. This is a CPU analysis of the saved pre-update scores from all 20 updates; no training was launched. It measures the loss derivative with respect to selected-token log probability, not parameter-gradient norms or optimizer displacement.

Among 25,528 positive-advantage teacher-token occurrences, 3,089 belong to the measured name/creator spans. Define a rare occurrence as student conditional probability below 1e-4. There are 694 such identity-token occurrences, spanning 409 of 1,055 positive-advantage identity spans. These spans include reasoning and quotations as well as final-answer assertions. The threshold is a diagnostic choice, not an evaluation success threshold.

| Local derivative diagnostic | Rare identity tokens | Other teacher tokens in the same response rows |
|---|---:|---:|
| Token occurrences | 694 | 22,439 |
| Median coefficient multiplying absolute advantage | 2.41e-6 | 0.222 |
| Median absolute derivative before reduction | 2.40e-6 | 0.213 |
| Exactly zero due to ratio clamp | 105 | 2 |

The comparator includes positive-advantage non-identity teacher tokens in any row containing a teacher identity span, whether or not that span contains a rare token. In this run that includes all 22,439 positive non-identity teacher tokens. The rare-token median coefficient is about 92,000 times smaller. Their summed unreduced local derivative magnitude accounts for 0.000557% of that sum across positive teacher tokens. This sum does not apply each update’s token-mean denominator and is not a measured fraction of the reduced training objective’s gradients. This scalar sum does not measure parameter-gradient directions, cancellation, or the eventual optimizer update. The result establishes weak direct supervision at the selected log probabilities; it does not prove how much of the observed weight movement comes from surrounding prose.

There is also a hard cutoff. The ratio primitive first clamps `student_logprob - teacher_logprob` to [-20, 20]. Below -20, autograd through that clamp is zero. This affects 105/694 rare positive identity-token occurrences (15.1%): 86 occurrences of ` Marin`, 18 of ` Athena`, and one of ` Snow`. The affected tokens can still move through shared-weight updates from other positions. The clamp therefore does not prove permanent inability to learn, but it removes their own direct teacher correction at these points. Twenty-five clamped occurrences remain in the last five batches; the issue is not confined to initialization.

Holding logits, data and advantages fixed, reducing gamma from 0.5 to 0.05, 0.005 or 0.0005 raises the rare-token median coefficient from 2.41e-6 to 2.41e-5, 2.40e-4 or 2.39e-3. These are algebraic counterfactuals, not training outcomes. Changing gamma alone leaves the hard-clamped derivatives at zero; removing only the clamp leaves most of the small-ratio suppression in place.

### Will more steps solve it?

There is evidence for slow progress, not a demonstrated plateau. All 13 repeated exact contexts whose initial target-sequence log probability is below -10 show an increase. Their endpoint slopes range from 0.018 to 0.348 natural-log units per update. However, nine contexts have only two observations and four have three. A fitted asymptote is not identifiable from this evidence.

For a concrete scale estimate, linearly extrapolate log probability to a diagnostic 1% probability for one exact target continuation after a fixed prefix. This is insufficient by itself to establish reliable identity behavior, excludes alternative spellings, and assumes the supplied prefix is already generated. It is not a forecast of 1% or any other held-out success rate.

The table uses least-squares regression over all three observations. Total updates means updates since initialization. The endpoint estimate below instead uses only each context’s first and last observation.

| Exact context | Observed updates | Linear estimate of total updates to 1% | In-sample R² |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Open-Athena after “I was created by” in the OpenPipe question | 1, 8, 14 | 142 | 0.995 |
| Marin Snowball after “I'm” in the OpenAI-model question | 4, 11, 17 | 181 | 0.973 |
| Marin Snowball after “I'm” in the GPT-4 question | 4, 11, 17 | 244 | 0.863 |
| Open-Athena after the creator prefix in that GPT-4 answer | 4, 11, 17 | 86 | 0.981 |

Across all 13 contexts, the extrapolated totals range from about 83 to 273 updates for twelve contexts and about 1,635 for the remaining context. The median endpoint estimate is another 97 updates after each context's last observation. These extrapolations extend far beyond the 20-step observation window. R² describes the three observed points and does not establish forecast reliability. Sampling selection, evolving advantages and prompts, parameter sharing, and changing ratios can all alter the trajectory.

Engineering judgment, not a calibrated behavioral forecast: I would not expect another 20 unchanged updates to resolve the problem. Under the fitted trends, those 20 updates would leave all 13 measured continuations below the diagnostic threshold. The roughly 100–300-total-update scale comes from the conditional log-probability fits; it suggests that some continuations could become appreciably more likely, but does not predict when held-out identity answers would emerge. Reliable held-out identity behavior and preservation remain unproven at that horizon. At the measured 7.69 minutes per update including periodic evaluation, 100–300 total updates would take roughly 13–38 hours on 48 H100s if throughput stayed constant. The objective continues to supervise surrounding tokens during that time. The present preservation holdout is too small to establish the safety of that longer exposure.

Recommendation: fix or ablate the low-support teacher-loss behavior before a long run. Test a formulation that retains a meaningful positive-reward teacher signal on rare identity tokens, while explicitly handling the ratio clamp; do not interpret teacher tokens as ordinary on-policy student samples. Compare against the current objective using a fixed held-out identity-token probe and the same behavioral evaluation. Merely raising the learning rate does not directly address the measured local coefficient imbalance; parameter-update effects also depend on the model Jacobian, clipping and the optimizer. No additional run or code change has been launched from this analysis.

Reproduction: run `artifacts/scripts/probe_identity_gradient_support.py` and `artifacts/scripts/project_identity_probability_trends.py` with the campaign CPU Torch environment at `artifacts/worktrees/marinskyrl/.venv/bin/python`. The first reads trusted campaign pickles and differentiates the runtime's ratio primitive; the second fits only exact-context matches. [Gradient summary](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-GRPO-Results/blob/38bdf19218a347f1f718ff47a7ac82a27dc8e256/analysis/pilot-filtered-20-v1/identity-gradient-summary.json), [token evidence](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-GRPO-Results/blob/38bdf19218a347f1f718ff47a7ac82a27dc8e256/analysis/pilot-filtered-20-v1/identity-gradient-tokens.jsonl), [span evidence](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-GRPO-Results/blob/38bdf19218a347f1f718ff47a7ac82a27dc8e256/analysis/pilot-filtered-20-v1/identity-gradient-spans.jsonl), and [projection details](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-GRPO-Results/blob/38bdf19218a347f1f718ff47a7ac82a27dc8e256/analysis/pilot-filtered-20-v1/identity-probability-projections.json) retain the counts, runtime primitive hash and limitations.
